scope: All iOS all-features launch evidence, including automated tests, human E2E, live service checks, device captures, professional reviews, store submissions, operations, and incident drills.

evidenceRecord.integrity: Hash retained artifacts after redaction. Hashes prove the retained redacted artifact, never the unretained sensitive original.
evidenceRecord.truthRule: A generated flag, checkbox, screenshot, simulator result, or local test cannot claim live, physical-device, professional, production, Apple-review, or staffed-operations evidence.

redaction.default: Collect the minimum evidence needed, redact before it enters the repository, chat, issue tracker, packet, or long-term store, and verify the redacted artifact cannot be reversed.
prohibitedContent: passwords, MFA or recovery codes, CAPTCHA answers, access or refresh tokens
private keys, signing certificates with private material, webhook secrets, service-role keys, database passwords
full payment, banking, tax, government identity, or identity-verification records
raw auth identifiers, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, precise location, device advertising identifiers
health answers, pregnancy status, user routines, private notes, community drafts, support content, or other user content
photo pixels, thumbnails, local photo paths, encryption keys, ciphertext samples, face data, or biometric artifacts
provider payloads or console screenshots that expose project secrets or personal account data
approvedSubstitutions: stable non-reversible evidence-local labels such as tester-A
last four characters only when needed to distinguish a non-secret identifier
cropped console state with account chrome and values removed
aggregate counts meeting documented minimum cohorts
hashes of approved source/review artifacts after secret scanning
captureProcess: capture into an access-restricted temporary location
remove prohibited data and irrelevant screen regions
inspect metadata, filenames, OCR text, logs, network bodies, and thumbnails
copy only the approved redacted artifact to its evidence directory
securely delete the temporary capture and record the redaction actions
redaction.failureRule: If safe redaction cannot be proven, retain a signed result record and non-secret external reference instead of the artifact.

rules.disposition: Delete after the defect is verified closed unless a legal hold or incident preservation rule applies.

rules.defaultReview: one year after the applicable app version is no longer supported
rules.disposition: Retain the redacted manifest, results, hashes, and minimum supporting artifacts; delete redundant raw captures earlier.
Retain submission, approval, release, rollback, and production-verification records until an approved legal retention schedule authorizes deletion.

rules.defaultReview: at each annual legal/data-retention review and whenever reviewed source changes
rules.disposition: Retain signed decision, authority/credential verification reference, exact source hashes, scope, conditions, expiry, and revocation history under the counsel-approved schedule.

rules.defaultReview: only under the applicable legal, tax, insurer, processor, or security schedule
rules.disposition: Legal-schedule-required; do not invent a deletion date or delete during a legal hold.

requirements: Every evidence record has one retention class and an explicit deleteOrReviewAt value.
Retention is not consent to collect more data; minimize first.
Deletion includes working copies, exported archives, issue attachments, temporary plaintext, and processor copies where contractually controllable.
A legal hold overrides normal deletion and is recorded without placing privileged legal advice in the repository.
Country-specific durations remain an external legal decision and must be recorded before production launch.

rules: Networked and high-risk features fail closed through a production kill switch only after their enabled state has passed launch gates.
Never roll back a database migration until forward/backward schema and data compatibility are proven on a restored staging copy.
EAS Update rollback must match runtimeVersion and cannot repair native code, entitlements, privacy manifests, or binary-only defects.
Account deletion, privacy rights, payment state, and owner-scoped data must remain available or fail safely during rollback.
Rollback completion requires the same privacy, smoke, monitoring, and owner-isolation checks used to declare recovery.

severities.definition: active private-data exposure, cross-account access, credential/signing compromise, unsafe health guidance at scale, incorrect charges at scale, destructive data loss, or launch-wide outage
severities.response: page the named incident lead immediately; contain or disable the affected surface; preserve minimal evidence; notify required decision owners

severities.definition: serious security/privacy/safety/payment defect or a critical launch flow unavailable without a safe workaround
severities.response: same-day staffed response, prevent further harm, and prepare rollback/repair

severities.definition: material degradation with a safe workaround and no known private-data, safety, or payment harm
severities.response: triage into the current release window with monitored mitigation

severities.definition: minor defect, documentation gap, or cosmetic issue with no material user harm

rules: Do not promise a regulatory, contractual, or user notification deadline without the named privacy/legal decision owner; record the decision and governing jurisdiction.
Do not place privileged advice, secrets, raw user data, or exploitable detail in public incident records.
P0/P1 closure requires root cause, affected scope, evidence integrity, corrective actions, recurrence controls, owner, deadline, and verification.
A production surface without a named staffed escalation owner remains launch-blocked.
